backups.name: Skyline Divide Route
hazards: Loose rock and talus on the final Class 2/3 scramble to the summit.
Residual snow on the ridge crest into early summer creates slip-and-fall hazard on steep side-hill terrain.
Route-finding difficulty in poor visibility, since the trail fades to an unmarked boot-path along much of Chowder Ridge.
backups.overview: The more popular of Hadley Peak's two standard approaches, following the well-known Skyline Divide trail up onto the ridge crest and then continuing cross-country along Chowder Ridge to the base of Hadley's summit block for a long, scenic ridge-walk scramble.
backups.beta: From the Skyline Divide Trailhead, a rugged, eroded trail switchbacks through forest to the ridge crest at about 2 miles, then rolls over a series of knolls along the open crest to the trail's high point (~6,563 ft) at about 4.5 miles. From there the maintained tread fades into a boot-packed path that continues along the open ridge crest for roughly another 3 miles, crossing minor ups and downs on Chowder Ridge, before reaching the base of Hadley Peak's final scramble. The last push is Class 2 with a short Class 3 step, climbing loose scree and talus to the summit; exposure is generally minimal for experienced parties.
backups.turnaround: Because the final scramble involves loose rock and a short exposed step, parties should set a turnaround time that leaves ample daylight and margin for slower downclimbing, and should not push onto the summit block in wet, icy, or low-visibility conditions.
backups.face: Northwest Ridge (Chowder Ridge - Hadley Peak connecting ridge)
backups.permit: Free self-issue Mount Baker Wilderness permit or trailhead registration; no quota or fee. Northwest Forest Pass at developed trailheads.
backups.comms: Cell coverage is unreliable in this area; no dependable service should be expected along the ridge — carry a satellite communicator for emergencies.
backups.descent: Reverse the ascent: downclimb the loose summit scramble back onto the ridge crest, then follow Chowder Ridge and the Skyline Divide trail back to the trailhead.

timing.recommendedStart: Pre-dawn/early-morning start given the long ridge day

backups.detailed_rack: None — this is a non-technical class 2-3 scramble with no roped climbing; no rack, rope, or protection is used.
what_to_bring: Recreation/day-use pass or annual Interagency pass for the trailhead
self-issue wilderness permit from the trailhead box
extra water/treatment (little to no reliable water on the ridge)
layers for exposed, wind-prone ridge walking
pro_tips: The ridge route is long and mostly unshaded — start early to beat both heat and afternoon thunderstorm risk on the exposed crest.
Parties describe the trail fading into a boot-path partway along Chowder Ridge; carry a GPS track or map, since route-finding in cloud/fog on the open ridge can be tricky.
Budget significant extra time for the up-and-down undulation of the ridge crest — GPS-tracked hikes commonly log more gain (3,300+ ft) than simple trailhead-to-summit elevation math would suggest.
watch_out: FS Road 37 is closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 while the 2021 washout at milepost 3.1 is repaired, making the Skyline Divide Trailhead inaccessible by vehicle — check current Forest Service alerts before planning this approach.
Loose scree and talus on the final summit push; a short Class 3 step near the top has real exposure.
Snow can linger on the ridge into July, requiring an ice axe and self-arrest skill on the traverse.
backups.pro_needs: No fixed protection or rope is used on the standard scramble line; the main 'gear' concern is footing on loose rock and residual snow, for which an ice axe is recommended in early or late season.
backups.best_season: Best from mid-summer through early fall once snow has cleared from the ridge and ambient mosquito pressure has dropped; the trail itself is usually snow-free by July, but lingering snow on the ridge traverse and lower-elevation mosquitoes in early season are common complaints in trip reports.
backups.approach: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS 39); turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37). FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead. FS 37 has been closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 since 1 June 2026 while the 2021 flood washout at milepost 3.1 is repaired, with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026, so the trailhead is not reachable by vehicle. When open, hike Skyline Divide Trail #678 through old-growth forest switchbacks and into meadows on the ridge crest (~2 mi), follow the crest to the trail's high point (~6,563 ft, ~4.5 mi), then continue cross-country along the open ridge to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley Peak.
backups.descent_text: From the summit, carefully downclimb the short Class 3 step and the loose scree/talus below it back to the base of the summit block. Retrace the boot-packed path along Chowder Ridge and the open ridge crest (roughly 3 miles) back to the trail's high point (~6,563 ft), then descend the maintained Skyline Divide Trail #678 through meadows and forest switchbacks to the trailhead.
backups.bail: The ridge route can be abandoned at nearly any point by simply retracing the ridge crest and trail back toward the Skyline Divide Trailhead; there is no fixed rappel or technical retreat required.

pitch_detail.notes: Trailhead through forest to Skyline Divide meadows (Trail #678), ~2 miles
Along Skyline Divide ridge crest to ~6,563 ft, ~2.5 miles of established trail
Cross-country south along the ridge to the Chowder Ridge junction
Chowder Ridge traverse on an established boot-path; mild exposure, side-hilling on steep slope
Final northwest-ridge summit block; loose rock, hard class 3 scrambling to the small, exposed summit

backups.itinerary: Typically done as a long single-day car-to-camp-free outing (when the trailhead is reachable): early trailhead start, roughly 4–5 hours to the summit along the ridge, and a similar time back down; some parties break it into an overnight with a ridge-camp on Chowder Ridge given the length (~14–15 miles round trip).

access.fees: $5/vehicle day-use fee at the trailhead, or annual Recreation/Interagency Pass
access.rules: Pack out human waste (blue bags) — no burial or glacier deposition. The route stays inside Mount Baker Wilderness, where party size is capped at 12 and campfires are prohibited.
access.permit: Free self-issue wilderness permit available at the trailhead
access.closures: Skyline Divide Trailhead is not reachable by vehicle: FS Road 37 (Deadhorse Road) has been closed at mile 0.03 since 1 June 2026 for flood-damage repair, with heavy equipment on the road and no end date given, as listed on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026.
access.landManager: USDA Forest Service, Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mount Baker Wilderness)
access.land_manager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at most trailheads — $30/year or $5/day.
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass or other accepted Interagency Pass

overnight_permit.where: No climbing or wilderness permit. A recreation pass is needed to park at the Skyline Divide trailhead; buy it ahead or on the Recreation.gov app.

road.name: Deadhorse Road (Forest Service Road 37)
road.status: Closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 since 1 June 2026 while flood-damage repair is under way, with no end date given, as listed on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026
road.driveNote: From Glacier, drive SR 542 east about 1 mile, turn right onto Glacier Creek Road (FS 39), then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37); FS 37 normally continues 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide Trailhead, but has been gated at mile 0.03 for flood-damage repair since 1 June 2026, with no end date given.
road.seasonalGate: No routine seasonal gate reported for FS 37 itself; access is presently blocked by the repair closure regardless of season

climate.fall: Often clear and dry with fewer bugs, but shorter daylight and increasing chance of early-season snow by October.
climate.spring: Ridge typically still snow-covered; not the standard scramble season.
climate.summer: Trail generally snow-free by July, but biting insects are heavy through July and August and the best window runs mid-August into early October; the ridge traverse can hold patchy snow into early July.
climate.winter: Full winter mountaineering/avalanche conditions; not the standard scramble route in winter.
climate.typical: Wet, maritime North Cascades weather with rapid changes possible even in summer; the exposed ridge crest is prone to wind and fast-moving cloud.
climate.forecastZone: NWAC West Slopes North (Mount Baker area)

emergency.notes: No reliable cell coverage along FR 37 or on the ridge; carry a satellite communicator.

seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: Mid-August through September, once Chowder Ridge's side-hill snow is gone and the mosquitoes have eased

July.reason: The trail usually clears in July, but lingering snow on the Chowder Ridge side-hill is a slip hazard and mosquitoes are at their worst.

June.reason: Snow usually still covers the upper road and the trailhead area, and the ridge side-hills hold steep snow.

August.reason: The ridge is usually snow-free by mid-August and the bugs drop off, leaving a long but straightforward approach to the scramble.

October.reason: Often still dry early in the month, but the long ridge day meets short daylight and the first snow can coat the side-hill.

November.reason: Early-winter snow covers the exposed ridge crest and the road to the trailhead may not be passable.

September.reason: Dry scree, few bugs and settled weather; the long day still fits the shortening daylight.

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From Glacier, WA, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS 39); turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (FS 37).

approach_variants.name: Skyline Divide Trail #678 and the long open ridge south to Chowder Ridge
approach_variants.notes:
ACCESS FIRST: from Glacier, WA drive SR-542 about a mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (FS-39), turn right, then immediately left onto Deadhorse Road (FS-37). FS-37 normally runs 12.7 miles to the Skyline Divide trailhead. FS-37 has been closed to vehicles at mile 0.03 since June 1, 2026 while the 2021 flood washout at milepost 3.1 is repaired, with no end date given on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on September 26, 2026, so the trailhead is not reachable by vehicle. Confirm before planning around it.

When open, Skyline Divide Trail #678 climbs through old-growth switchbacks into meadows and reaches the ridge crest at about 2 miles and its high point near 6,563 ft at about 4.5 miles. From there the route is cross-country along the open ridge — roughly three miles of it — to Chowder Ridge and the base of Hadley's summit block.

The trail's high point on the crest near 6,563 ft is the landmark parties use to re-find the maintained trail on the way back.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Aug-Oct — this trailhead may not currently be reachable at all
hazards: FS-37 closed at mile 0.03 during washout repair — the trailhead is not drivable until the work ends
Three miles of cross-country open ridge with no tread and no cairns
A short Class 3 step above loose scree and talus
Two unmarked divides converging on one summit, with very different roads at the bottom
No water once past the meadows
approach_variants.baseFinding:
THE 6,600 FT VIEWPOINT IS THE GATE, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. It is where maintained trail ends and where you rejoin it. In cloud it is the only reliable waypoint on this approach, because everything beyond it is three miles of undifferentiated open ridge. Note it on the way out — parties who do not, spend the return walking a crest that all looks the same.

THE CREST IS THE HANDRAIL. From the viewpoint the route runs SOUTH along the ridge and then SOUTHEAST along Chowder Ridge, roughly three miles in all. Keep the crest under your feet with air on both sides; this ridge has heather benches falling away either side and it is easy to drift onto one and lose the line.

ARRIVAL AT THE CLIMBING: the summit block is a SHORT CLASS 3 STEP above loose scree and talus — the last stretch of the day and the only scrambling on it. Walking stops, one short step of rock, summit. That is the whole climb, and it is the test: if you are scrambling for a long time, you are on a false feature; if you have not left your feet, you are not there.

THE DISCRIMINATOR AGAINST THE OTHER APPROACH TO THIS SAME BLOCK: Cougar Divide arrives on Chowder Ridge from the NORTH-WEST after crossing near Dobbs Creek, and its trail high point is 5,920 ft. Skyline arrives from the WEST after roughly three miles of ridge from a 6,600 ft viewpoint. If you are descending in poor visibility, going down the wrong divide puts you 11 miles of gravel road away from your car on a road that may itself be washed out.

bivy.name: Skyline Divide crest camps
bivy.notes: The other approach to Hadley Peak, from the west along the divide and over Chowder Ridge. The road in has been the problem for years rather than the trail: flood damage at around mile three has left the trailhead inaccessible to vehicles for extended periods with no firm repair date, and the trail has been listed as closed on that account, so this is the first thing to confirm and not an afterthought. When it goes, the crest is easy walking with big views and the last three quarters of a mile up to Chowder Ridge is talus with one steeper step before you top out west of the Hadley Glacier. Camping on the open crest means taking whatever weather arrives off the mountain, and the exposure is the reason parties often drop into the basin instead.
bivy.water: None at the trailhead and none along the trail after early summer, when the snow patches below the crest are gone. Carry everything or plan the trip around a lingering snowfield you have confirmed is still there.
bivy.permit: Mt Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Mount Baker Wilderness. A recreation pass is required at the trailhead. No campfires anywhere, party size capped at 12, all waste packed out. There is no permit or quota for camping, but the meadows are heavily used and heavily damaged, so camp on bare ground.
bivy.capacity: Several exposed sites along the open crest of the divide once the trail tops out; popular and visible, with no screening from wind or weather

bivy.name: Deadhorse Creek basin, below Chowder Ridge
bivy.notes: The basin sits between Skyline Divide and Cougar Divide, just short of the climb onto Chowder Ridge, and it solves the problem both crest camps have: it has water and it has shelter. A party approaching Hadley from either road can drop into it, sleep out of the wind, and take the ridge in the morning with full bottles. Summit day from here is short by any standard on this mountain. It is subalpine meadow and creek terrain, so camp on durable ground well back from the water. Season is the same as everything else on the north side, mid-August into early October, held back at the front end by mosquitoes and by the road gate on the Cougar Divide side and at the back end by the first real snow.
bivy.water: The most reliable water on the Hadley approach — the creek runs from snowmelt above the basin and holds up later than anything on the ridge crests. Treat it. This is the reason to camp here rather than higher.
bivy.permit: Mount Baker Wilderness, no overnight permit required. Recreation pass at whichever trailhead you start from. Party size 12, campfires prohibited, human waste and everything else packed out — there are no toilets on either divide.
bivy.capacity: Scattered informal sites in the basin between the two divides; sheltered, low use, no facilities of any kind
